name: Iliff Senior Apartments
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: MGL Partners is building Iliff Senior Apartments (marketed as Iliff Apartments), a 50-unit, four-story rental for adults 62 and older at 30% to 80% AMI on a former office site at E. Iliff Avenue and S. Dahlia Street in Denver's University Hills, financed with 2024 Round One 9% and state housing tax credits.
why_it_matters: It shows a 9% senior deal on a bought-and-demolished office site using income averaging, including 80% AMI units, plus a Denver linkage-fee loan and an Impact Development Fund land loan; the city loan closed in June 2025 and construction started in August 2025.

status.label: Under construction since August 2025; completion was expected September 2026 (not confirmed)
status.detail: Denver's HOST loan closed on 2025-06-11 (per a city resolution request), and MGL announced the groundbreaking on 2025-08-20 with completion expected in September 2026. No public record of completion, a certificate of occupancy or lease-up was found as of 2026-10-21.

next_step: Watch for a Denver certificate of occupancy and leasing notices from MGL or Silva Management Partners for 4750/4770 E. Iliff Ave.

key_numbers.meaning: 44 one-bedroom and 6 two-bedroom units for ages 62+, averaging 55% AMI; the 5 units at 80% AMI were underwritten at 65% AMI rents.

key_numbers.value: $1,396,651 a year in federal 9% credit plus $700,000 of state credit
key_numbers.meaning: About $14.0M in federal credit over 10 years (inferred from the annual amount).
Approved by Resolution 25-0711 on 2025-05-19, paid from the Affordable Housing Linkage Fee Fund, with a covenant of at least 60 years.
MGL's estimate at groundbreaking (August 2025); the 2024 application estimated $24,008,384.

background.text: Land: MGL contracted to buy the Bethesda Professional Office Building Condominium (built 1983) for $2.7M (about $54,000 per unit) with a June 2024 closing; Mile High CRE reported the purchase complete on 2024-07-08. The office building was to be demolished after NEPA review, with about $100,000 budgeted for demolition and asbestos abatement.

Zoning was by right; the project entered Denver's Affordable Housing Review Team expedited process. In June 2025 Denver dedicated city-owned parcels at E. Iliff Ave. and S. Dahlia St. as public right-of-way (Resolution 25-0737), inferred to be related frontage work.

Income averaging: units at 30%, 40%, 50%, 60% and 80% AMI average 55% AMI. The applicant says these would be the only 61-80% AMI senior tax credit units in the market area; the market study flagged 50% and 60% AMI capture rates above CHFA's 25% guideline.

City loan: Denver council adopted Resolution 25-0711 on 2025-05-19 approving a $2.25M HOST loan to Iliff Senior Apartments LLLP; the city's later request says the loan closed 2025-06-11 and that rental restrictions are secured by a covenant of at least 60 years.
Groundbreaking was announced 2025-08-20, with the cost estimated at $25.8M and completion expected in September 2026.

The application estimated $24,008,384 ($480,168 per unit) in total cost, with a 1.19 debt coverage ratio, and said the tax credit partnership would close and construction start within 13 months of award.

discrepancies.text: CHFA, the application and Denver's loan documents give the address as 4770 E. Iliff Ave., while the groundbreaking coverage gives 4750 E. Iliff Ave.
The application lists $2,000,000 of HOST cash-flow debt, while the loan Denver approved is $2,250,000.

The application says the Denver Housing Authority would be special limited partner to provide the sales, use and property tax exemption, while groundbreaking coverage names Eaton Senior Communities as the special limited partner providing the property tax exemption.
Denver's resolution 25-0711 gives the HOST loan term as 240 months, while the attached request form and the later amendment request give 270 months.
